newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar hits 125 yen in Tokyo, highest in 50 months.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hits 125 yen in Tokyo, highest in 50 months.

text.p: The dollar hit the key level of 125 yen in Tokyo on Monday, its highest since February 1993, buoyed by rising U.S. interest rates and reassuring words from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
The dollar rose despite a jump in Japan's current account surplus for February, announced earlier on Monday.

The rise was also despite rumours in financial markets earlier that the Ministry of Finance had called major Japanese life insurers and suggested they not buy dollars, and that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) called around banks enquiring about rates in a bid to discourage more dollar buying.
But there was no sign of intervention by the BOJ to sell dollars, action which would tend to slow the yen's fall.

Traders said Japanese investors bought strongly, taking advantage of a recent rise in U.S. interest rates. They said the market was also reassured by remarks by Rubin when he was in Japan last Friday, when he said that exchange rates should not be used as a tool to deal with Japan's trade surplus.
The market interpreted the statement as meaning that Washington still wants a strong dollar.
